newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 2.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky says wage developments can strongly affect inflation and the health of the crown.

In addition, higher wages mean higher costs for a company and, therefore lower competitiveness. Tosovsky also expects the inflation rate to decrease somewhat and the rate of GDP growth to increase in 1997. He declined to list the central bank's 1997 inflation targets.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told Czech television that he is wishing for more cooperation in the coalition in 1997. He also stated his conviction that economic growth would continue in the new year with growth of four or five percent.
- The profit of the big four Czech banks will be enough to ensure that the Czech banking sector will not finish 1996 in the red, according to the chairman of the banking association, Jiri Kunert.

- The union leader in Poldi Ocel has stated that the steel plant does not have enough funds to pay wages or to restart production and that some outside help will be needed to get out of the current situation.

- If privatisation will take place in the banking sector, then the total of foreign investment should increase in 1997. If there will be no banking privatisation, then a decrease of foreign investment is expected due to the current situation on the capital market, according to Martin Kupka from Patria Finance.

- According to a majority of filling stations in the Czech Republic, the price of petrol and diesel fuel will likely not decrease in 1997. Due to the gradual membership in the EU fuel prices could actually increase instead.

- Prazske Pivovary, the third-largest domestic brewing group, will open a new brewing plant during the course of 1997, increasing capacity from 1.2 to 2.2 million hectolitres of Staropramen beer a year. The new plant cost 200 million crowns while the total modernisation of the brewery should take a total investment of 1.2 billion crowns by 1998.

- ZS Brno a.s., one of the largest domestic construction firms is expecting sales for 1996 to increase by approximately 30 percent to 3.4 billion crowns. The company's gross profit should reach 45 miollion crowns, according to the company's general manager, Michal Stefl.

- Slovakia's state-owned DMD Holding, a group of the most important Slovak military companies, is expecting to sign a contract for mutual cooperationm with Skoda Plzen and CKD Praha, according to the director of Skoda Lubomir Soudek.
PRAVO - The economic prognoses for 1997 will likely be more pessimistic in the near future due to the poor economic results in 1997, according to a number of financial experts.

- The Chemofond investment fund decided to lower its basic capital by changing the nominal value from 1000 to 900 crowns. The change will help cover the company's losses of 39 million crowns from 1995.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The standard of living in the Czech Republic will likely improve in 1997 in spite of the pessimistic economic outlook. This is due to the fact that wages are expected to increase faster than consumer prices.
